The absolute value of each nontrivial cycle product is at most \(1-\zeta_0<1\), and every fixed-point factor is one. Thus every one of the \(p!\) Leibniz terms has absolute value at most one, whence
\[
|\det G|\leq p!.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(\sigma_1(G)=\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), the condition-number bound makes every other singular value at least \(\sigma_1(G)/\overline\kappa\). Therefore
\[
\frac{\sigma_1(G)^p}{\overline\kappa^{p-1}}
\leq\prod_{j=1}^p\sigma_j(G)=|\det G|\leq p!,
\]
so
\[
\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq L_0.
\tag{2}
\]
Since \(G_{ii}=1\), \(\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\geq1\), and hence
\[
\|G^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\overline\kappa/\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\overline\kappa.
\tag{3}
\]

\textbf{Compactness and the global residual gap.} Every defining condition of \(\mathfrak T\) is closed. Inverses are encoded by \(DU=UD=I_p\) and \(AV=VA=I_p\); cycle slack is a finite family of weak polynomial inequalities; affine separation is a finite conjunction of disjunctions of weak polynomial inequalities; and the PSD conditions \(\Omega,\Psi\succeq0\) and covariance-interiority conditions \(\Sigma_e,\Gamma_e\succeq\lambda_0I_p\) are closed. Equations (2)--(3) bound \(D,A,U,V\). Each scale inequality bounds the PSD nuisance, all covariance matrices, and every nonnegative shift coordinate on its side. Thus every fixed \((H_1,H_2,S)\)-piece is closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and is compact by \(\text{lem:compact-continuous-minimum}\). Their finite union \(\mathfrak T\) is compact, and its closed far subfamily \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) is compact.

If \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\neq\varnothing\), continuity of \(\mathfrak r\) and \(\text{lem:compact-continuous-minimum}\) give a minimizer. Suppose its residual were zero. Then on \(S\),
\[
D\Sigma_eD^{\mathsf T}=\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e),
\qquad
A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e),
\qquad e\in S.
\tag{4}
\]
For each \(k<\ell\), the first design's affine-separation constraint supplies a triple in \(S\) with affine minor of absolute value at least \(\gamma_0\); hence its \((k,\ell)\)-cloud on \(S\) is not contained in an affine line.

There are \(|E\setminus S|=m-q=2c\) remaining labels. Partition them into disjoint sets \(C_1,C_2\) of cardinality \(c\). Extend the first explanation to \(S\cup C_1\) by using zero shifts and covariance \(D^{-1}\Omega D^{-\mathsf T}\) on \(C_1\), and extend the second to \(S\cup C_2\) by using zero shifts and covariance \(A^{-1}\Psi A^{-\mathsf T}\) on \(C_2\). The nuisance matrices are only required to be PSD, so these auxiliary covariances are PSD; no positive-definiteness claim is needed. Both added shift vectors are nonnegative. The two fitted sets have size \(q+c=h\), intersect exactly in \(S\), and (4) makes the explanations agree there. The hypotheses of \(\text{lem:overlap-uniqueness}\), which accepts PSD invariant nuisances and covariance slots, now hold. It follows that \(A=D\). Since \(U=D^{-1}\), this gives \(AU=I_p\), contrary to \(\|AU-I_p\|_{\mathrm F}\geq\rho_0>0\). Therefore
\[
\mu_0>0.
\tag{5}
\]
The same conclusion holds by definition when the far family is empty.

All coefficients describing \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) are rational or effectively specified real algebraic numbers, and the latter have rational polynomial equations with isolating sign conditions. For rational \(d>0\), the assertion that some \(\tau\in\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) satisfies \(\mathfrak r(\tau)<d\) is first-order rational-polynomial after squaring the Frobenius-norm inequalities. It is decidable by \(\text{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\). By (5), the assertion is false for all sufficiently small dyadic \(d=2^{-j}\). Hence the search terminates and returns
\[
0<\underline\mu\leq\mu_0,
\qquad
r_0=\frac{\underline\mu}{2\sqrt p\,L_0^2}>0.
\tag{6}
\]

\textbf{Entry into the identity chart.} Fix \(A\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). Exactness of the released code from \(\text{thm:certified-inference-representation-obstruction}\) supplies \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\), matrices \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\), a nuisance \(\Psi\succeq0\), and nonnegative shifts \(t_e\) such that
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e),
\qquad e\in K.
\tag{7}
\]
The clean universal audit supplies the candidate-side affine separation, cycle slack, covariance interiority, condition number, and scale constraints. Inclusion--exclusion gives \(|H\cap K|\geq2h-m=q\); choose \(S\subseteq H\cap K\) with \(|S|=q\). On \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\),
\[
\|\Gamma_e-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq r_{n,\alpha,H},
\qquad e\in S.
\tag{8}
\]
Set \(U=D^{-1}\) and \(V=A^{-1}\). The theorem-local premise supplies \(\Omega\succeq0\); the three structural assumptions supply the normalization, covariance equations, and nonnegative shifts; and the five true-instance bounds supply the remaining true-side constraints. Thus these objects form a tuple in \(\mathfrak T\). From (2), (7), (8), submultiplicativity, and \(\|X\|_{\mathrm F}\leq\sqrt p\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left\|A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}-\Psi-\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\right\|_{\mathrm F}
&=\left\|A(\Sigma_e-\Gamma_e)A^{\mathsf T}\right\|_{\mathrm F}\\
&\leq\sqrt p\,L_0^2r_{n,\alpha,H}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
If \(\|AD^{-1}-I_p\|_{\mathrm F}\geq\rho_0\), the maximum of the left side of (9) over \(S\) is at least \(\mu_0\geq\underline\mu\); when \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\leq r_0\), (9) bounds it by \(\underline\mu/2\), a contradiction. Thus, with
\[
Q=AD^{-1}=I_p+R,
\qquad u=\|R\|_{\mathrm F},
\]
one has
\[
u<\rho_0\leq1,
\qquad K_0\overline M u\leq\frac12.
\tag{10}
\]

\textbf{Local inverse inequality.} Fix \(e_0\in S\) and write \(x_e=s_e-s_{e_0}\). For each \(i<j\), affine separation supplies a triple in \(S\) with determinant of absolute value at least \(\gamma_0\). Expanding that determinant into the three pairwise cross-products based at \(e_0\) and applying the triangle inequality supplies \(e,f\in S\) such that
\[
|x_{ei}x_{fj}-x_{ej}x_{fi}|\geq\gamma_0/3.
\tag{11}
\]
Let \(E_e=\Gamma_e-\Sigma_e\). Subtract the candidate equation (7) at \(e_0\) from its equation at \(e\), and likewise subtract the true covariance equations. The first differencing cancels \(\Psi\), and the second cancels \(\Omega\). Taking the \((i,j)\) off-diagonal entry of
\[
Q\operatorname{diag}(x_e)Q^{\mathsf T}
+A(E_e-E_{e_0})A^{\mathsf T}
\]
therefore gives
\[
R_{ij}x_{ej}+R_{ji}x_{ei}
=-\sum_{k=1}^pR_{ik}R_{jk}x_{ek}
-[A(E_e-E_{e_0})A^{\mathsf T}]_{ij}.
\tag{12}
\]
The scale bound and shift nonnegativity imply \(|x_{ek}|\leq\overline M\). Equation (8) gives \(\|E_e-E_{e_0}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2r_{n,\alpha,H}\), while
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|QD\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq(1+u)L_0.
\]
Thus (12), Cauchy--Schwarz, and \(\sum_k|R_{ik}R_{jk}|\leq u^2\) imply
\[
|R_{ij}x_{ej}+R_{ji}x_{ei}|
\leq\overline M u^2
+2r_{n,\alpha,H}L_0^2(1+u)^2.
\tag{13}
\]
Apply (13) at the two environments in (11) and solve the resulting two-by-two system. Since every coefficient \(|x_{ek}|\leq\overline M\) and the determinant is at least \(\gamma_0/3\), for every ordered pair \(i\neq j\),
\[
|R_{ij}|\leq\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma_0}
\left\{\overline M u^2
+2r_{n,\alpha,H}L_0^2(1+u)^2\right\}.
\tag{14}
\]
The unit diagonals of \(A\) and \(D\) give
\[
0=(A-D)_{ii}=(RD)_{ii}
=R_{ii}+\sum_{k\neq i}R_{ik}D_{ki}.
\tag{15}
\]
For each \(i\), the squared norm of the \(i\)-th column of \(D\) is at most \(L_0^2\). Summing the squared off-diagonal bounds in (14), applying Cauchy--Schwarz to (15), and taking square roots yields
\[
u\leq K_0\left\{\overline M u^2
+2r_{n,\alpha,H}L_0^2(1+u)^2\right\}.
\tag{16}
\]
By (10), the first term on the right of (16) is at most \(u/2\), and \((1+u)^2\leq4\). Hence
\[
u\leq16K_0L_0^2r_{n,\alpha,H}.
\tag{17}
\]
Finally,
\[
\|A-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=\|RD\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq uL_0
\leq16K_0L_0^3r_{n,\alpha,H}
=C_0r_{n,\alpha,H}.
\tag{18}
\]
Taking the supremum over \(A\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) proves the outer-radius bound. On the coverage event, \(D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) by \(\text{thm:certified-inference-representation-obstruction}\), so the union is nonempty. For \(A_1,A_2\) in it, the triangle inequality and (18) give \(\|A_1-A_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2C_0r_{n,\alpha,H}\), proving the diameter bound. The constants use only the fixed dimensions and five audit thresholds, which proves uniformity and the stated limits.

statements.statement: For \(p=2\), \(m=h=3\), and \(c=0\), let the three encoded covariance regions be the singletons containing \(\Sigma_1=2I_2\), \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(3,2)\), and \(\Sigma_3=\operatorname{diag}(2,3)\). Then \(\mathcal R_0(\Sigma)=\{I_2\}\). Every full feasible tuple has \(A=I_2\), \(\Psi=\operatorname{diag}(a,b)\) with \(a,b\in[0,2]\), and shifts \(t_1=(2-a,2-b)\), \(t_2=(3-a,2-b)\), and \(t_3=(2-a,3-b)\). Consequently \(\gamma=1\), \(\zeta=1\), \(\lambda_{\mathrm{cov}}=2\), \(\kappa=1\), and \(M\leq9\) for every feasible tuple, so \(\text{CertificateInferenceHandle}\) releases the exact singleton union at thresholds \((\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0,\overline\kappa,\overline M)=(1,1,2,1,9)\).
statements.justification: This exact rational example proves that a gauge-invariant covariance-interiority audit can release even though the invariant nuisance has a continuum of admissible diagonal gauges, including singular ones.
statements.gap: The example certifies nonvacuity of the universal audit; it is not a numerical implementation and does not replace the general contraction proof.
statements.consumer: It provides a regression-test instance for a future symbolic or numerical corruption-aware BACKSHIFT workflow.
statements.proof_tex:
Write a normalized candidate as
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&u\\v&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Any feasible explanation must congruence-diagonalize both covariance differences. Since
\[
\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,0),
\qquad
\Sigma_3-\Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(0,1),
\]
their transformed off-diagonal entries are, respectively,
\[
\left[A\operatorname{diag}(1,0)A^{\mathsf T}\right]_{12}=v,
\qquad
\left[A\operatorname{diag}(0,1)A^{\mathsf T}\right]_{12}=u.
\]
Feasibility forces both to vanish, so \(u=v=0\) and \(A=I_2\). Conversely, \(I_2\) is feasible. Indeed, for any \(a,b\in[0,2]\), take
\[
\Psi=\operatorname{diag}(a,b),
\]
\[
t_1=(2-a,2-b),\qquad
t_2=(3-a,2-b),\qquad
t_3=(2-a,3-b).
\]
Then \(\Psi\succeq0\), every shift is nonnegative, and \(\Sigma_e=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\). Conversely, once \(A=I_2\), the off-diagonal covariance equations force \(\Psi\) to be diagonal; writing it as \(\operatorname{diag}(a,b)\), PSD feasibility gives \(a,b\geq0\), while nonnegativity of all three shifts gives \(a,b\leq2\). Thus the displayed family is exactly the set of nuisance gauges and \(\mathcal R_0(\Sigma)=\{I_2\}\).

The three shift points are
\[
(2-a,2-b),\qquad(3-a,2-b),\qquad(2-a,3-b),
\]
whose affine determinant is one. Since \(h-c=3\), the definition gives \(\gamma=1\). Also \(\operatorname{CP}(I_2-I_2)=0\), so \(\zeta=1\), and \(\kappa(I_2)=1\). The least covariance eigenvalue is two, hence \(\lambda_{\mathrm{cov}}=2\). Finally,
\[
M
=1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\max_e\|\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\max_e\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq1+2+3+3=9.
\]
Every full feasible tuple therefore passes the five thresholds \((1,1,2,1,9)\). The singleton regions have finite rational-semialgebraic codes. Exactness and termination from \(\text{thm:certified-inference-representation-obstruction}\), together with the universal bounds just proved, therefore make \(\text{CertificateInferenceHandle}\) release the union \(\{I_2\}\).

statements.statement: For a finite complete family of real symmetric matrices that is exactly simultaneously diagonalizable by congruence, the randomized SDC algorithm of He and Kressner diagonalizes the family with probability one. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), under the paper's regularity condition, if the complete family is \(\varepsilon\)-close to an SDC family, then with high probability the algorithm diagonalizes it with error of norm \(\mathcal O(\varepsilon)\).

source.verbatim_statement: RSDC achieves diagonalization with probability 1 if the family is exactly SDC. Under a mild regularity assumption, given a family that is epsilon-close to SDC then RSDC diagonalizes, with high probability, the family up to an error of norm O(epsilon).

statements.gap: It perturbs a complete family memberwise and does not study adversarial replacement of entire environment slots or confidence-union inversion.
statements.consumer: It fixes the boundary between standard robust SDC recovery and this paper's whole-environment replacement contribution.

sampling_model.design: There are \(m\) labeled environments; an unknown set \(H\) of size \(h=m-c\) follows one population BACKSHIFT covariance model and the remaining \(c\) slots are arbitrary elements of \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\).
sampling_model.units: For population identification only \(\Sigma_e\) is observed. At each index \(n\), every slot supplies an independent within-environment sample of size \(n\) used to construct the indexed simultaneous covariance region \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown additive shift interventions have diagonal covariance \(\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\); intervention targets and strengths are not observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The two candidate honest subsets may overlap in only \(m-2c=h-c\) slots.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance is estimated for the population theorem. Compatibility permits an invariant nuisance in \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\); the sharp converse and conditioning analysis impose the explicit interior condition \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\). The inference layer propagates indexed honest-slot simultaneous covariance regions through feasibility-oracle constraint inversion and measures all perturbations in operator norm.

estimand_functional: For a fixed honest design \(D,H,s\) and \(\Sigma\in(\mathbb S_+^p)^E\), let robust recovery mean that \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every positive-semidefinite assignment to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). For every \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\), \(\delta_H>c\) implies robust recovery without an invertibility condition on the honest covariances. If the fixed instance has \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\), robust recovery holds if and only if \(\delta_H>c\), and failure is realized by positive-definite replacements. Thus \(\delta_H>c\) is minimax sharp over the published positive-semidefinite covariance and invariant-noise class, with failure witnessed in its positive-definite subclass.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The population BACKSHIFT solution is unique exactly when every pair of intervention-variance profiles is noncollinear.
An exact non-unitary joint diagonalizer is essentially unique if and only if the diagonal-profile collinearity modulus is below one.
Outlier target matrices are omitted by iteratively retaining matrices whose geometric residual is below a chosen threshold.

Theorem 1 gives noiseless unique topology identification when the exogenous-covariance factor has Kruskal rank at least two, nonzero edges are continuously distributed, and at least two off-diagonal nonzero entries are known in every column.
Simultaneous diagonalizability by congruence of a complete Hermitian family is equivalent to positive-definite feasibility of a linear matrix system.
Pairwise environment comparisons identify causal structure with high probability under probabilistically sparse mechanism changes.

The randomized SDC algorithm exactly diagonalizes an exactly SDC complete symmetric family with probability one and, under its regularity condition, achieves high-probability \(\mathcal O(\varepsilon)\) diagonalization error when every member of the family is within \(\varepsilon\) of an SDC family.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The audited contraction treats arbitrary replacement of \(c\) whole environments, competing size-\(h\) subsets with only \(m-2c\) shared slots, BACKSHIFT normalization, PSD common nuisances, nonnegative raw shifts, the sharp adversarial replacement radius, and confidence-union inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Local perturbation sensitivity for an already selected approximate joint diagonalization problem is controlled by its uniqueness and conditioning quantities.
Identification-robust tests and confidence sets maintain uniform asymptotic size across weak and strong identification regimes.

tldr: Unknown shift interventions identify a cyclic linear causal system because covariance differences share a non-unitary congruence diagonalizer. The field-tier kernel asks how many entire covariance environments may instead be arbitrary. The structural matrix satisfying the BACKSHIFT unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization survives every \(c\)-slot positive-definite replacement if and only if deleting the largest affine-line subset from every pairwise honest shift cloud costs more than \(c\) environments. The converse uses the explicit interior condition on invariant noise to produce a legal positive-definite contamination and a second cycle-product-normalized system. A generic sparse-support formula turns the distance into a combinatorial design criterion; finite subset enumeration is only a reduction to an exact feasibility oracle, while operator-norm contraction of indexed confidence unions, rational certificates, and mandatory abstention at zero affine separation remain the computational agenda for updating the CRAN pooled-difference workflow.

project_justification.gap: Published BACKSHIFT identifies from an entirely honest environment family, general joint-diagonalization theory studies one complete matrix family, and existing outlier-aware joint diagonalization uses a tuning threshold without an exact adversarial radius.
project_justification.niche: Whole-environment replacement creates a discrete overlap geometry: two explanations may discard different slots and therefore share only \(m-2c\) covariance matrices. Affine rather than linear collinearity is the invariant obstruction because the common nondiagonal noise covariance disappears only after differencing.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the necessary-and-sufficient distance \(\delta_H>c\), a matching positive-definite contamination witness satisfying the BACKSHIFT cycle-product normalization under the interior-noise condition, and the exact generic support-incidence formula. Finite subset enumeration is recorded only as a definitional feasibility-oracle implementation note. The open inference target asks for explicit operator-norm radius and modulus functions for indexed confidence unions on fixed-margin uniform classes, rational certificates, chart switching, and abstention at vanishing affine minors.

related_work: The field-tier radius result is informed by RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 and its appendix proof, which supplies the all-honest model, pairwise profile reduction, and cycle-product normalization; its generic-amplitude result is Corollary 2(ii). KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, informs the complete-family uniqueness step through profile collinearity.
